correctness.rationale: A one-cap half has adjacent endpoints; after removing it the propagating identification is the increasing bijection between the two ordered complements. If |j−k|≤1, the two middle arcs coincide or meet and do not create new exterior caps, giving 3n−5 middle choices at each rank-(n−2) target. If disjoint they each pull back to a cap in an exterior half, so the rank falls exactly two. A two-cap half is disjoint adjacent D or nested consecutive N, as no unmatched strand can pass under a cap; the propagating strands then match uniquely in order. Transfer along the ordered complements gives four branches for D, two for N; substitution of the other middle index gives the complementary inequality pairs in the proof and hence the four target formulas. More explicitly, the correction is the equality count between multisets {a,b−2} for D and {a} for N, and the constant is the product of their sizes. For D,D any three of four equality matches force the fourth; the two crossed equalities together require b=a+2, d=c+2, and a=c. The other five pair intersections each have d=m(m+1)/2 elements; one- and two-equality incidences then give the full histogram. Positivity proves that all target diagrams of both ranks occur; the sum of the lower counts is [n(n−3)/2]^2 and their weighted sum is (n−3)(n−2)(n−1)^2. Independent ordered-complement transfer reproduced every lower target and the census for 4≤n≤20. The size 7 is absent only in the rank-decreasing class (the rank-preserving fiber is 7 at n=4). There are four lower targets at n=4, six occupied fiber sizes at n=5, and seven occupied sizes exactly for n≥6; the zero entries of the displayed table handle the small n cases. The all-n result is combinatorial, not extrapolated from the checks.
